## MUTATION LEDGER — six mutations, all RED, and the load-bearing one proves the guards carry the weight

Run by the orchestrator INLINE rather than by a subagent: two agents stalled on this worktree (watchdog,
600s no progress), and the second stalled at exactly this step. Each mutation was applied to the
IMPLEMENTED source, the module re-run, then the file restored from the byte-verified backups in
`/tmp/88d9-bak/` — **`git checkout --` was never used.** Every mutation was verified to have actually
applied before its verdict was believed (an unapplied mutation yields a false GREEN, so the harness
asserts the write landed). Baseline and post-restore both **16 passed**.

Module: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_parent_clear_88d9.py` (16 tests).

| mutation | file | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **M6 UNCONDITIONAL CLEAR** — all three guards stripped at once | inbound_fields.py | **4 failed, 12 passed** |
| M1 layer-1 revert: a None parent leaves the field ABSENT again | fetcher.py | 3 failed, 13 passed |
| M2 UNOBSERVED treated as NO_PARENT | inbound_fields.py | 2 failed, 14 passed |
| M3 UNRESOLVABLE treated as NO_PARENT | inbound_fields.py | 1 failed, 15 passed |
| M4 managed gate bypassed | inbound_fields.py | 1 failed, 15 passed |
| M5 `"parent": "parent_id"` removed from `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` | inbound_differ.py | 2 failed, 14 passed |

No verdict was an `AttributeError` / `ImportError` / `TypeError`, so every RED is an oracle refusing
behaviour rather than a mutation breaking wiring.

### M6 IS THE RESULT THAT MATTERS — an unconditional clear is a DATA-LOSS BUG that the happy path CANNOT SEE

FAILED under M6 — exactly and only the four guard oracles:
    test_unobserved_parent_emits_no_clear
    test_degraded_parent_map_emits_no_clear
    test_unresolvable_parent_key_emits_nothing
    test_unmanaged_parent_is_adopted_not_clobbered

STILL PASSING under M6 — including **both** oracles one would naively trust:
    test_observed_parentless_emits_the_clear          <- the HAPPY PATH
    test_end_to_end_a_removed_jira_parent_leaves_parent_id_empty   <- the END-TO-END oracle
    (plus test_unchanged_parent_does_not_churn, test_reparent_still_emits_the_new_parent,
     test_never_parented_issue_never_emits_a_parent_mutation, test_same_pass_outbound_parent_write_
     suppresses_the_clear, test_outbound_parent_translates_to_the_inbound_parent_id_name, and 5 more)

So a fix that clears the parent unconditionally — deleting local parents off truncated and failed reads —
**passes the happy-path AND the end-to-end assertion.** Only the guards catch it. That is the whole
argument for the guard oracles existing, demonstrated rather than asserted.

Verbatim guard messages:

    a parent clear was emitted for an issue the parent map NEVER MENTIONED — a truncated or
    cross-project read would silently delete the local parent: {'DC-1': {'parent_id': None}}

    a FAILED parent-map read (the {} degradation contract) cleared the local parent — the exact
    silent data loss this ticket exists to prevent: {'DC-1': {'parent_id': None}}

    an UNRESOLVABLE Jira parent key emitted a parent_id mutation. Jira has a parent — it is merely
    unbound this pass — so neither a clear nor a set is correct

    an UNMANAGED parent was cleared. rebar never managed this ref, so its local presence is not
    evidence we ever pushed it and the clear clobbers local state

### The two ACs that are easiest to under-deliver are both satisfied

 * **End-to-end**: `test_end_to_end_a_removed_jira_parent_leaves_parent_id_empty` exists and asserts the
   REDUCED TICKET's `parent_id` is empty — not merely the differ's output. (And note it is NOT sufficient
   on its own: M6 shows it passing while the code is a data-loss bug.)
 * **No hand-mirrored production copy**: layer 1 was EXTRACTED as
   `fetcher.merge_parent_map(snapshot, parent_map)`, a directly-callable production helper whose docstring
   states the three-state contract, and the tests drive THAT. This is the lesson bought by 2b16, whose G1
   evidence rests on `_enrich_like_fetcher` — a byte-faithful hand copy that will silently drift. M1
   mutating the real helper and turning 3 tests RED is the proof the tests are wired to production code.

### Implementation shape, for the record

`classify_inbound_parent` returns one of four explicit states — `PARENT_UNOBSERVED` (no `parent` key),
`PARENT_NO_PARENT` (key PRESENT and falsy: queried, Jira genuinely has none), `PARENT_RESOLVED`,
`PARENT_UNRESOLVABLE` — and `diff_inbound_parent` emits the clear only for `PARENT_NO_PARENT`, gated on the
shared `should_propagate_removal`, the same provider-agnostic predicate the outbound side wraps as
`_parent_clear_is_managed`. Reused, not re-invented.

LOC, all under the 800 cap: **inbound_differ.py 797 → 773 (NET NEGATIVE — layer 2 was extracted, not
inlined, which was required since it had only 3 lines of headroom after 2b16), inbound_fields.py 247 → 351,
fetcher.py 670 → 707.**

### KNOWN BLIND SPOT, recorded not hidden

`add_managed_ref` is folded by the parent-set EVENT (`reducer/_processors.py:90,528`), so "managed" means
the ref was set LOCALLY — it does NOT prove Jira ever had that parent. The same-pass suppression closes
this in a healthy pass, and it genuinely fires for parent because `_OUTBOUND_TO_INBOUND_FIELD` maps
`"parent" → "parent_id"` (M5 proves a test catches that entry's removal). The residual window is a DEGRADED
pass — outbound not writing the parent while inbound proceeds. **Read 2b16's latest comment before
assuming this suppression is enough: on the LINK side the analogous same-pass guard turned out to suppress
every legitimate peer-deletion mirror.** The parent case differs (an outbound parent SET is emitted only
for an epic parent, per 39c1's disjoint gates, so it does not fire on every peer clear the way a link ADD
does) — but that asymmetry is a reason to verify on the harness, not to assume.
